userStories.title: Classify terminal native account and credential errors
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recover SDK-embedded failure statuses and classify terminal account and credential errors without transport retries.

**Motivation** — With no `TOGETHER_API_KEY` and no stored credential, a `together` request yields `{kind: "transport", message: "Provider is not configured: together"}`.

**Approach** — **Failure classification (nax-ai).**
- Recover the status an SDK printed into the message. pi-ai produces three spellings: the Anthropic SDK path writes `<status> <body>` (`402 {"type":"error",...}`), `formatProviderError` on the OpenAI-completions path writes `<status>: <body>` (`401: {"type":"authentication_error",...}`), and a bodiless failure reads `429 status code (no body)`. A new exported helper `statusFromSdkMessage(message: string | undefined): number | undefined` in `packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/errors.ts` returns the leading status when the message matches `/^([45]\d\d):? (\{|status code)/`, and `undefined` otherwise. The `error` case in `createPiProtocol`'s event loop calls it **only when `observed?.status` is `undefined`**. It passes the recovered status to `classifyProviderError` and reports it as the event's `status`. An observed status always wins over a recovered one. Accepted consequences: a recovered 503 becomes `overloaded` and a recovered 408/409 `bad-request`, both previously retried as `transport`; a plain-text body (`401 Unauthorized`) is not recovered and stays `transport`.
- `classifyHttpError(402)` returns `"quota"`: payment required means the account cannot pay, and waiting does not help.
- `classifyBrokenStream` (non-failing or absent status) checks a new credential-marker table **before** `STREAM_POLICY_MARKERS`. A message containing `provider is not configured` or `no api key for provider` (case-insensitive) is `"auth"`.
- `QUOTA_MESSAGE_PATTERN` accepts an underscore as well as a space: `insufficient[ _](credits|quota|balance)`. The twin `QUOTA_PATTERN` in `packages/nax/src/agents/errors/parse-agent-error.ts` changes identically, because the file comments require the two to stay in step.

Downstream needs no change. `packages/nax-agent/src/native/errors.ts` already maps `quota` to `fail-quota` (not retriable) and `auth` to `fail-auth` (not retriable). `failurePolicyFor` grants terminal backoff only to `fail-rate-limit`, `fail-stale` and `fail-service-down`.

Baseline: `createPiProtocol` `case "error"` uses `const status = observed?.status`. Target: `const status = observed?.status ?? statusFromSdkMessage(event.error.errorMessage)`. Keep abort, usage and retry-after behavior intact, and omit the event's status property when no status exists. Add the new pi-client-error-status.test.ts with fake PiDeps driven through the real protocol stream. The classifyHttpError table has no 402 row today; add `[402, "quota"]` while every existing row keeps its expected kind. Show regression tests failing against old code before implementation.

**Scope** — In: nax-ai error classification and protocol event status recovery. Out: US-002 owns the ACP quota-regex twin; US-003 owns provider registration; US-004 owns credential gate/forwarding; US-005 owns URL validation and warnings. The 402 status recovery is not applied to thrown errors (`classifyThrown`), which already read `status` off the thrown object. Do not change downstream retry/failure policy.

**Interface** — `statusFromSdkMessage(message: string | undefined): number | undefined`; `classifyHttpError(402)` returns `"quota"`; `classifyProviderError(undefined, message)` recognizes credential markers before stream policy markers.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] classifyHttpError(402) returns "quota".
[unit] statusFromSdkMessage('402 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"insufficient_balance_error","message":"insufficient balance (1008)"}}') returns 402.
[unit] statusFromSdkMessage("429 status code (no body)") returns 429.

[unit] statusFromSdkMessage("500 tokens were generated before the stream broke") returns undefined.
[unit] statusFromSdkMessage(undefined) returns undefined.
[unit] classifyProviderError(undefined, "Provider is not configured: strata") returns "auth".
[unit] classifyProviderError(undefined, "No API key for provider: strata") returns "auth".
[unit] classifyProviderError(429, "insufficient_balance: top up your account") returns "quota".

[unit] When createPiProtocol over fake deps is driven through stream and deps.stream emits a pi error event whose errorMessage is '402 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"insufficient_balance_error","message":"insufficient balance (1008)"}}' without invoking onResponse, the protocol yields one error event with kind: "quota" and status: 402.

[unit] When createPiProtocol over fake deps streams an error after onResponse reports status 200, with errorMessage '402 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"insufficient_balance_error","message":"insufficient balance (1008)"}}', its error event has status: 200 and kind equal to classifyProviderError(200, message); the observed status wins over the recovered one.

[unit] When createPiProtocol over fake deps streams a pi error event with errorMessage "Provider is not configured: strata" and no onResponse call, its error event has kind: "auth" and no status property.

[unit] When createPiProtocol over fake deps streams a pi error event with errorMessage '401: {"type":"authentication_error","message":"missing or wrong API key"}' and no onResponse call, its error event has kind: "auth" and status: 401.

[unit] When createPiProtocol over fake deps streams a pi error event with errorMessage '429: {"error":{"message":"slow down"}}' and no onResponse call, its error event has kind: "rate-limit" and status: 429.
[unit] When a createPiProtocol error event has no observed status and errorMessage '429 {"error":{"message":"slow down"}}', its yielded error has kind: "rate-limit" and status: 429.

[unit] When retryTransportFaults wraps a protocol yielding a recovered 402 quota error before any content, it returns that error without starting another attempt.

routing.reasoning: Two existing source modules and focused regression tests; status precedence and credential classification are security-sensitive, requiring strict test/implementation isolation.

When a credential marker and a rate-limit policy marker coexist under an absent or 200 status, classifyProviderError returns "auth".
When an error event has no observed status and errorMessage "503 status code (no body)", createPiProtocol emits kind: "overloaded" and status: 503.
When an error event has no observed status and errorMessage "408 status code (no body)" or "409 status code (no body)", createPiProtocol emits kind: "bad-request" with the corresponding status.

userStories.title: Keep ACP quota wording synchronized
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Recognize underscore-delimited insufficient-balance quota wording in nax's ACP error helper.

**Motivation** — MiniMax-M3 with an empty balance returns an error event with `kind: "transport"` and message `402 {"type":"error","error":{"type":"insufficient_balance_error","message":"insufficient balance (1008)"}}`.

**Approach** — `QUOTA_MESSAGE_PATTERN` accepts an underscore as well as a space: `insufficient[ _](credits|quota|balance)`. The twin `QUOTA_PATTERN` in `packages/nax/src/agents/errors/parse-agent-error.ts` changes identically, because the file comments require the two to stay in step.

Widen `QUOTA_PATTERN` in `packages/nax/src/agents/errors/parse-agent-error.ts` to `insufficient[ _](credits|quota|balance)`, the twin of nax-ai's `QUOTA_MESSAGE_PATTERN`.

Modify only the nax twin here; US-001 changes nax-ai's pattern. `parse-agent-error-quota.test.ts` gains cases but no existing assertion changes. Preserve plain rate-limit, per-minute quota and structured-parser behavior. Show the underscore regression failing against the old code.

**Scope** — In: QUOTA_PATTERN and focused isQuotaMessage regressions. Out: US-001 owns native SDK-status recovery and classification; US-003/004/005 own custom provider support. The ACP agent error parser in nax (`parse-agent-error.ts`) changes only its quota wording. Recovering an SDK status from ACP stderr is not part of this feature.

**Interface** — `isQuotaMessage(message: string): boolean`; `QUOTA_PATTERN` uses `insufficient[ _](credits|quota|balance)` while retaining all its other alternatives.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] isQuotaMessage('{"error":{"type":"insufficient_balance_error","message":"x"}}') returns true.
[unit] isQuotaMessage("insufficient balance (1008)") returns true.
[unit] isQuotaMessage("Rate limit exceeded, please slow down") returns false, preserving the existing distinction between a transient rate limit and account quota exhaustion.

routing.reasoning: A localized quota regex change with existing helper tests; no authentication, session or credential behavior changes in this story.

userStories.title: Introduce custom native providers in nax-ai
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Register explicitly declared unknown providers with their own auth, supported wire backends and openrouter thinking format.

**Motivation** — The override list is process-global (`getNativeClient` builds one client), so one override for `strata` makes the native client unbuildable for every model.

**Approach** — **Custom providers (nax-ai).**
- `ProviderOverride` (`packages/nax-ai/src/providers/types.ts`) gains `readonly authEnv?: string`.
- In `applyOverrides` (`packages/nax-ai/src/protocols/pi-client.ts`), when `models.getProvider(override.provider)` is `undefined`, the override **introduces** a provider instead of throwing, provided all of these hold:
  - `override.baseUrl` is declared.
  - Every model's `protocol` is `"openai-completions"` or `"anthropic-messages"`.
  - Every model declares `maxTokens`. There is no sibling to inherit a ceiling from.
  - `models` is non-empty.
  - No earlier entry in the same override list introduced the same provider id (two entries for one new id are rejected rather than letting the second be read as an amendment).
  The existing per-model checks `assertOverrideModelProvider`, `assertOverrideModelRouting` and `assertOverrideModelThinkingFormat` run on introduced models exactly as on amended ones.
- The introduced provider is built with pi-ai's `createProvider` (exported from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/models`). It takes `id` and `name` equal to the override's provider id, the override's `baseUrl` and `headers`, and an `api` map keyed by protocol holding the result of calling each lazy API factory the models use: `openAICompletionsApi()` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-completions.lazy` and `anthropicMessagesApi()` from `@earendil-works/pi-ai/api/anthropic-messages.lazy`. It also takes `auth` (below) and `models` (the synthesised models below). It is registered with `models.setProvider`.
- Its `auth.apiKey` is `envApiKeyAuth(override.provider, override.authEnv !== undefined ? [override.authEnv] : [])`, exported from the `@earendil-works/pi-ai` root (the same helper pi's bundled `together` provider uses). A stored credential's `key` wins. Otherwise the value of the environment variable named by `authEnv` resolves. Otherwise it returns `undefined`, so pi reports the provider unconfigured and the event classifies as `auth` (above). The variable is read at dispatch through pi's `ctx.env`, the same ambient read pi's bundled providers make for their own key variables; nax's config boundary validates only the variable's name, not its presence (precheck warns when it is unset).
- Each introduced model is synthesised without a template. Its fields:
  - `id` and `name` are `model.id`; `api` is `model.protocol`; `provider` is the override id; `baseUrl` is the override's; `input` is `["text"]`.
  - `contextWindow` and `maxTokens` come from the model; `cost` is `toPiCost(model.pricing)`.
  - `reasoning` follows the same expression `synthesiseModel` uses today.
  - `compat` carries only a declared `thinkingFormat` / `openRouterRouting`.
  - `thinkingLevelMap` is `model.thinkingLevelMap ?? deriveThinkingLevelMap(model, undefined)`.
  - `reasoning` is true whenever a non-`off` level is declared, so pi's `openrouter` branch fires.
  - When the override declares `headers`, `headers` is a copy of them.
- `packages/nax-ai/README.md` (which says an override cannot introduce a provider) is updated to describe introduced providers.
- All pi-ai imports stay in `pi-client.ts` (`check:pi-ai-imports` allows only `pi-client.ts`, `pi-catalog.ts` and `pi-auth.ts`). nax-ai has no file-size gate, so `pi-client.ts` may grow.
- The client-side catalog (`normaliseCatalog`) already creates a model bucket for an unknown provider, so `client.model("strata", id)` resolves today. It is unchanged.

**Override rules for an existing provider are unchanged**, with one addition: `authEnv` on an override whose provider pi-ai already knows throws, naming the provider. Replacing a bundled provider's credential resolution is not this feature.

**`thinkingFormat: "openrouter"`.** It is added to nax-ai's `ThinkingFormat` union, nax-agent's `CatalogModelOverride.thinkingFormat` union and nax's `CatalogModelOverrideSchema` enum. nax-ai already places a declared `thinkingFormat` on `compat` verbatim. `deriveThinkingLevelMap(model, undefined)` leaves `off` unset, so pi's `openrouter` branch sends `reasoning: {effort: "none"}` at `off`. No wire code changes; the value only becomes declarable.

This story implements only the nax-ai portion of the thinkingFormat change; US-004/005 own their respective mirrors. Preserve isolated catalog caching and all existing-provider amendment behavior. The existing test case "throws at construction for a provider the backend catalog does not know" declares no baseUrl, so it must still throw. Keep it and keep its totally-made-up regex match; if wording changes only its matcher may change and must still require the provider id. Create pi-client-custom-provider.test.ts rather than expanding the already-large existing override test file. Show regressions failing against old code.

Fixture STRATA is a ProviderOverride with provider: "strata", baseUrl: "http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1", authEnv: "STRATA_TEST_KEY", and models: [{ id: "qwen3.8-flash", provider: "strata", protocol: "openai-completions", contextWindow: 262144, maxTokens: 32768, supportsTools: true, thinkingLevels: ["off", "low", "medium", "high"], thinkingFormat: "openrouter", pricing: { input: 0, output: 0, cacheRead: 0, cacheWrite: 0 } }]. Tests that set STRATA_TEST_KEY restore its previous process-environment value afterwards. The injected fakeStreamSimple replaces pi's dispatch only; the apiKey it receives comes from nax-ai's auth resolver over the introduced provider's auth. Use createMemoryCredentialStore with nax-ai credentials, not pi's credential shape. The real payload assertions use pi's openai-completions streamSimple and onPayload with intercepted/no-network fetch, following the existing override test's normalizeContext pattern. Important interface clarification: streamSimple accepts SimpleStreamOptions.reasoning, not OpenAICompletionsOptions.reasoningEffort. To exercise the spec's absent reasoningEffort case omit reasoning; to exercise reasoningEffort low pass reasoning: "low", which streamSimple translates to the lower-level reasoningEffort. Do not pass an ignored reasoningEffort property to streamSimple or change pi wire code.

**Scope** — In: nax-ai ProviderOverride.authEnv, ThinkingFormat, provider registration/model synthesis, auth precedence and README. Out: US-001 owns terminal error classification, US-004 owns config-to-client forwarding/credential availability, US-005 owns URL security/schema/precheck and user docs. `nax auth login <custom-provider>` and `nax auth import` for an introduced provider are not added: login enumerates pi-ai's builtin providers. An introduced provider authenticates from its `authEnv` variable, or from a credential already stored under its id. Keyless servers get no special path. An introduced provider with no resolvable key fails as `auth`. A server that needs no key is used by setting the `authEnv` variable to any placeholder value, as Strata's docs advise for OpenAI SDK clients. Introduced providers support only `openai-completions` and `anthropic-messages`. `openai-responses` and every other pi protocol are rejected at construction. `authEnv` cannot replace the credential resolution of a provider pi-ai already bundles; that combination is rejected.

**Interface** — `ProviderOverride` gains `readonly authEnv?: string`; `ThinkingFormat` gains `"openrouter"`; `applyOverrides(models, overrides)` introduces valid unknown ids through `models.setProvider`, rejecting invalid introductions with provider-naming errors. Auth is `envApiKeyAuth(override.provider, override.authEnv !== undefined ? [override.authEnv] : [])`.

[unit] resolveModel("qwen3.8-flash", "strata") on createPiDeps({ providerOverrides: [STRATA] }) resolves to a model whose baseUrl is "http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1", api is "openai-completions", provider is "strata" and maxTokens is 32768.

[integration] When createClient is called with defaultProviders(), the defaultProtocols factory and providerOverrides: [STRATA], client.model("strata", "qwen3.8-flash") resolves to a ResolvedModel with provider: "strata" and protocol: "openai-completions".

[unit] createPiDeps with two override entries both introducing provider "strata" throws an error whose message contains "strata".
[unit] resolveModel("qwen3.8-flash", "strata") for STRATA returns a model whose reasoning is true.

[unit] When the resolved STRATA model is passed to pi's real openai-completions streamSimple, imported from @earendil-works/pi-ai/api/openai-completions as pi-client-overrides.test.ts does, with no reasoningEffort (omit the public streamSimple options.reasoning field) and an onPayload hook, the captured payload has reasoning equal to { effort: "none" }.

[unit] When the same real openai-completions streamSimple call requests reasoningEffort: "low" by passing its public option reasoning: "low", the captured payload has reasoning equal to { effort: "low" }.

routing.reasoning: New behavior-bearing provider registration, no-template model synthesis and real backend payload integration cross the catalog/auth seam; credential precedence mandates strict security TDD.

suggestedCriteria: When a custom provider declares only an anthropic-messages model with baseUrl and maxTokens, createPiDeps resolves that model with api: "anthropic-messages" and the declared output ceiling.
When an introduced provider's model claims a different provider id, createPiDeps throws an error naming both provider ids.
When an introduced anthropic-messages model declares thinkingFormat: "openrouter", createPiDeps throws an error naming the model and protocol.
Given a client with an introduced provider and a separate client without that override, resolving the introduced model on the latter fails as an unknown model.
When the STRATA_TEST_KEY value changes after createPiDeps construction but before dispatch, dispatch resolves the new value.
When an introduced model declares thinkingLevelMap explicitly, resolveModel returns that map rather than replacing it with derived entries.
When an introduced provider declares headers and the caller subsequently mutates its input header object, the resolved model retains the original header values.

userStories.title: Forward custom provider auth and recognize its credentials
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Carry custom provider declarations through nax-agent and keep a custom-only native adapter eligible when its authEnv is set.

**Motivation** — The current workaround hijacks the bundled `together` provider: `baseUrl` points at a local proxy and the local key is exported as `TOGETHER_API_KEY`.

**Approach** — **Forwarding (nax-agent).** `ProviderCatalogOverride` (`packages/nax-agent/src/config/catalog-overrides.ts`) gains `authEnv?: string` and `allowInsecureHttp?: boolean`. The second exists so nax's parsed config (and the `catalogOverrides` result of `collectConfiguredModelPins`, typed `readonly ProviderCatalogOverride[]`) can carry the flag to precheck; nax-agent never acts on it and `toProviderOverrides` does not forward it. `toProviderOverrides` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/models.ts`) forwards `authEnv` as `...(override.authEnv !== undefined ? { authEnv: override.authEnv } : {})`, never `undefined`.

Here, the conditional spread forwards authEnv only, not allowInsecureHttp. Add `"openrouter"` to `CatalogModelOverride.thinkingFormat`, matching upstream US-003.

**Credential gate (nax-agent).** `NativeSessionAdapter.hasCredentials` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/session-adapter.ts`) answers today from the owned store, an exec auth source, stored providers, or `anyAmbientCredential()`, which probes only pi's bundled providers. A run whose only native provider is introduced would be pruned by `validateAgentCredentials` (`AGENT_CREDENTIALS_MISSING`). Target: before the ambient probe, `hasCredentials` returns true when any of the adapter's `catalogOverrides` declares an `authEnv` whose variable is non-empty, read through a new `_adapterDeps.readEnv(name)` seam defaulting to a `process.env` lookup.

Read-only wiring: `buildNativeClient` (`packages/nax-agent/src/native/client.ts`): passes `toProviderOverrides(catalogOverrides)` as `providerOverrides`, and the same array reaches `_clientDeps.defaultProtocols({ providerOverrides, ... })`.

Codebase finding: _adapterDeps is declared in native/adapter-deps.ts and imported by session-adapter.ts; add readEnv to that existing object, not a second object. Preserve the existing owned-store, exec-source, stored-provider and fail-open-on-probe-error semantics. nax-agent.api.txt lists exported names only, and no name changes; the new tests live in a new file. US-003 -> US-004 seam: ProviderOverride.authEnv is produced by toProviderOverrides, pinned by the buildNativeClient spy and the real-wire request URL/Authorization assertion. Use test/unit/native/provider-overrides.test.ts; follow the existing nax#2019 client.test.ts intercepted-fetch pattern. Restore all patched seams, fetch, temporary credential-store state and process environment. Show regressions failing before implementation.

**Scope** — In: agent catalog types, authEnv forwarding, openrouter mirror and custom credential availability. Out: US-003 owns custom-provider registration/auth resolution; US-001 owns classification; US-005 owns HTTP validation, warning decisions, config descriptions and user docs. nax-agent must not enforce or forward allowInsecureHttp. `authEnv` cannot replace the credential resolution of a provider pi-ai already bundles; that combination is rejected upstream.

**Interface** — `ProviderCatalogOverride` gains `authEnv?: string` and `allowInsecureHttp?: boolean`; `CatalogModelOverride.thinkingFormat` gains `"openrouter"`; `toProviderOverrides` forwards `...(override.authEnv !== undefined ? { authEnv: override.authEnv } : {})`; `_adapterDeps.readEnv(name)` defaults to process.env lookup; `NativeSessionAdapter.hasCredentials` returns true for a declared authEnv with a non-empty value before calling the ambient probe.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] toProviderOverrides([{ provider: "strata", baseUrl: "http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1", authEnv: "STRATA_KEY", models: [one valid model] }]) returns one override whose authEnv is "STRATA_KEY".
[unit] toProviderOverrides on an override without authEnv returns an override object that has no authEnv property.
[unit] Given an override whose models array contains a model declaring thinkingFormat: "openrouter", toProviderOverrides([override])[0].models[0].thinkingFormat is "openrouter".
[unit] toProviderOverrides on an override declaring allowInsecureHttp: true returns an override object that has no allowInsecureHttp property.

[integration] With _clientDeps.defaultProtocols replaced by a spy, buildNativeClient([a strata override with authEnv: "STRATA_KEY"]) invokes the spy once with providerOverrides[0].authEnv equal to "STRATA_KEY".

[integration] Given STRATA_KEY="k-wire" (restored afterwards) and globalThis.fetch replaced by an interceptor that records each request and answers 401, streaming qwen3.8-flash of provider strata through buildNativeClient([{ provider: "strata", baseUrl: "http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1", authEnv: "STRATA_KEY", models: [one openai-completions model with maxTokens] }], { transportRetries: 0 }) records exactly one request whose URL starts with "http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1/chat/completions" and whose Authorization header is "Bearer k-wire", following the existing nax#2019 wire test in client.test.ts.

[unit] Given a NativeSessionAdapter constructed with catalog overrides [a strata override with authEnv: "STRATA_KEY"], _adapterDeps.authSourceIsExec resolving false, listStoredProviders resolving [], anyAmbientCredential resolving false and readEnv returning "k" for "STRATA_KEY", hasCredentials() returns true.

[unit] Given a NativeSessionAdapter constructed with catalog overrides [a strata override declaring authEnv: "STRATA_KEY"], _adapterDeps.authSourceIsExec resolving false, listStoredProviders resolving [], anyAmbientCredential resolving false and readEnv returning undefined for "STRATA_KEY", hasCredentials() returns false.

routing.reasoning: Existing mapper/type/seam patterns span five source files with a real dispatch regression; session credential eligibility and bearer forwarding require strict security TDD.

suggestedCriteria: Given no owned, exec, stored or ambient credential and readEnv returning an empty string for every declared authEnv, NativeSessionAdapter.hasCredentials() returns false.
Given several catalog overrides and only a later override's authEnv is non-empty, NativeSessionAdapter.hasCredentials() returns true.
Given a non-empty custom authEnv value, NativeSessionAdapter.hasCredentials() returns true without invoking anyAmbientCredential.

userStories.title: Expose secure custom provider configuration and warnings
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Validate custom provider fields, explicitly opt into remote plaintext endpoints, and surface credential-source/destination warnings.

**Motivation** — A Strata server on `http://192.168.1.175:8080/v1` (Strata serves plain http only) is a config load error.

**Approach** — **Config and precheck (nax).**
- `ProviderCatalogOverrideSchema` gains two fields:
  - `authEnv`: an optional environment-variable name matching `/^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*$/`. It is named after `commandSafety.shadow.authEnv` and deliberately not `apiKeyEnv`: `nax config` masks any key matching `API_?KEY`, which would hide the variable name.
  - `allowInsecureHttp`: an optional boolean.
- A new exported predicate `isRemotePlainHttp(url: string): boolean` in `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-model.ts` (exported through the `@/config` barrel) returns true exactly when the URL parses, its scheme is `http:`, and its hostname is not in the existing `LOOPBACK_HOSTS` set (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `::1`). Both the schema rule and the precheck below call it; neither re-derives the loopback decision.
- The per-field `isSafeBaseUrl` refine becomes an object-level `superRefine` (pattern: `CommandSafetyShadowSchema` in `packages/nax/src/config/schemas-command-safety.ts`) so it can read the flag:
  - userinfo is always rejected;
  - `https:` is accepted;
  - `http:` to a loopback host is accepted;
  - `http:` to any other host is accepted only when `allowInsecureHttp === true`;
  - every other scheme is rejected.
  The rejection message for remote http names the flag: `... set allowInsecureHttp: true to send this provider's credential over plain http`.
- A new file `packages/nax/src/precheck/checks-catalog-endpoints.ts` exports `checkCatalogEndpoints(catalogOverrides, env)`. It returns warning-tier `Check` rows, and `checkModelResolution` appends them (keeping that function's complexity flat):
  - **insecure-http warning**: for each override with `allowInsecureHttp === true` whose `baseUrl` is `http:` to a non-loopback host. The message names the provider and the host and says the credential is sent unencrypted.
  - **authEnv-unset warning**: for each override with `authEnv` whose variable is unset or empty in `env`. The message names the provider and the variable.
  - **authEnv-destination warning**: for each override with both `authEnv` and `baseUrl`, one row naming the provider, the variable and the `baseUrl` host, saying that variable's value is sent as the bearer credential to that host. This is the `authEnv` counterpart of the existing nax#2019 stored-credential redirect warning: a project-level config could otherwise point any secret-holding variable at any host without a visible line.
  
  `env` is supplied by a new `_modelResolutionDeps.env` seam defaulting to `process.env`.
- `FIELD_DESCRIPTIONS` gains `agent.native.catalogOverrides.authEnv` and `agent.native.catalogOverrides.allowInsecureHttp`. The `.baseUrl` description and the `.thinkingFormat` description (which gains `'openrouter'`) are updated.
- `docs/guides/configuration.md` gains a custom-provider example (a `strata` override with `baseUrl`, `authEnv`, `allowInsecureHttp`, and a model with `thinkingFormat: "openrouter"`).

**`thinkingFormat: "openrouter"`.** It is added to nax-ai's `ThinkingFormat` union, nax-agent's `CatalogModelOverride.thinkingFormat` union and nax's `CatalogModelOverrideSchema` enum. nax-ai already places a declared `thinkingFormat` on `compat` verbatim. `deriveThinkingLevelMap(model, undefined)` leaves `off` unset, so pi's `openrouter` branch sends `reasoning: {effort: "none"}` at `off`. No wire code changes; the value only becomes declarable.

Implement only nax's enum mirror here; upstream mirrors are US-003/004. US-004 -> US-005 seam: ProviderCatalogOverride.authEnv is the type nax's parsed config is passed as; pin it with schema round-trip assertions and the precheck seam through checkModelResolution. Extend ModelResolutionDeps with env and append helper rows before the existing empty-check success fallback. Warning rows have tier: "warning" and passed: false; multiple warning reasons for one override produce separate rows and never contain the environment variable's value. The insecure-http message must name allowInsecureHttp as well as provider/host. Keep strict schemas and all existing rejection/acceptance outcomes. Keep the existing case "rejects a plaintext http scheme" (http to gateway.test without the flag), and add a case asserting its error message names allowInsecureHttp. Add checks-catalog-endpoints.test.ts, exercise both direct helper results and integration through _modelResolutionDeps.env, restoring seams afterwards, and show new regressions failing against the old code. Root docs/guides/configuration.md is the explicit documentation exception to this story's binding packages/nax workdir; do not relocate it under the package.

**Scope** — In: nax schema/barrel predicate, openrouter enum, typed config round trips, precheck helper and env seam, field descriptions and configuration guide. Out: US-001/002 own error classification; US-003 owns provider registration/auth resolution; US-004 owns agent forwarding/hasCredentials. `nax-agent-acp`'s server config (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/nax-config.ts`) keeps reading `catalogOverrides` as untyped records. Switching the user's own `~/.nax/config.json` from the `together` proxy workaround to a `strata` override is a manual step after release, not a story.

analysis:
Goal and completion: enable native custom providers under their own ids, expose openrouter thinking declarations end-to-end, make remote plaintext HTTP a visible per-override opt-in, and stop treating terminal account/credential failures as transport faults. This is an enhancement to three existing TypeScript packages, not a new subsystem. Exactly five binding stories are retained: US-001 and US-003 in packages/nax-ai, US-002 and US-005 in packages/nax, US-004 in packages/nax-agent; dependency chain US-003 -> US-004 -> US-005, with US-001 and US-002 independent. US-005 retains its mandated packages/nax workdir even though its documentation update is the repository-root docs/guides/configuration.md. No implementation source has been changed during PRD drafting. Navigation: codebase-memory MCP is unavailable in this host, so findings were established by direct reads and text searches; no executable/test runner is exposed, so these findings are static verification, not a claim that tests or live requests ran.

Architecture and boundaries: packages/nax-ai/src/providers/types.ts:120 defines ThinkingFormat and :193 defines ProviderOverride; add openrouter and readonly authEnv respectively. packages/nax-agent/src/config/catalog-overrides.ts:68 mirrors catalog model types, :92 mirrors thinkingFormat, and :96 defines ProviderCatalogOverride. nax re-exports these agent types through packages/nax/src/config/schema-types.ts:123, consumes them in packages/nax/src/config/runtime-types-agent.ts:164, and parses the array through packages/nax/src/config/schemas-infra.ts:443. Keep the vocabulary synchronized without importing nax-ai into nax-agent/config or directly into nax config/precheck: the permitted consumer is agent/native. packages/nax/src/config/index.ts:143 re-exports model schemas and must also export isRemotePlainHttp. nax-ai shipped source remains Node ESM, has exactOptionalPropertyTypes, requires explicit .ts relative imports and forbids Bun APIs. Agent shipped source is also Node-compatible, with #src imports or explicit .ts relative imports; nax uses its existing Bun-oriented conventions. All new pi-ai source imports belong in pi-client.ts; the only other allowed adapters are providers/pi-catalog.ts and auth/pi-auth.ts. Do not add Anthropic OAuth, pricing-cost calculations, new public agent seam exports, dependency bumps or release changes. Root docs/architecture/ARCHITECTURE.md:11 indexes dependency injection, errors, constants and testing patterns; package instructions require red-before-green regression evidence. Strict three-session-tdd is selected for US-001/003/004/005 because they classify authentication, resolve credentials, gate sessions or authorize credential destinations; US-002 is a small regex change using tdd-simple.

US-005 complexity is reduced to medium because its object refinement, small predicate, Check helper and env seam use established local patterns; strict three-session-tdd remains required for credential-destination security. US-001/004 stay medium, US-002 simple, and US-003 complex for actual behavior-bearing provider/auth/backend integration.

Out-of-scope audit: all nine feature-level exclusions remain verbatim and separate in the top-level array: (1) no custom login/import flows, (2) no keyless special case, (3) only the two introduced-provider protocols, (4) no bundled auth replacement, (5) no ACP server config URL validation, (6) no ACP SDK-status recovery, (7) no message-status recovery for thrown errors, (8) no personal-config migration story, (9) no change to existing stored-credential redirect warnings. Near-boundary stories echo these exclusions without excluding their own implementation or other stories' required work. There are no story-local spec out-of-scope blocks to hoist. No executable JSON parser or test runner is available in this tool set; this audit re-read source/interfaces and reviewed the JSON edits, and does not claim runtime validation.
outOfScope: `nax auth login <custom-provider>` and `nax auth import` for an introduced provider are not added: login enumerates pi-ai's builtin providers. An introduced provider authenticates from its `authEnv` variable, or from a credential already stored under its id.

Keyless servers get no special path. An introduced provider with no resolvable key fails as `auth`. A server that needs no key is used by setting the `authEnv` variable to any placeholder value, as Strata's docs advise for OpenAI SDK clients.
Introduced providers support only `openai-completions` and `anthropic-messages`. `openai-responses` and every other pi protocol are rejected at construction.
`authEnv` cannot replace the credential resolution of a provider pi-ai already bundles; that combination is rejected.

`nax-agent-acp`'s server config (`packages/nax-agent-acp/src/server/nax-config.ts`) keeps reading `catalogOverrides` as untyped records. It does not validate `allowInsecureHttp` or the baseUrl scheme.
The ACP agent error parser in nax (`parse-agent-error.ts`) changes only its quota wording. Recovering an SDK status from ACP stderr is not part of this feature.
The 402 status recovery is not applied to thrown errors (`classifyThrown`), which already read `status` off the thrown object.
Switching the user's own `~/.nax/config.json` from the `together` proxy workaround to a `strata` override is a manual step after release, not a story.
The existing nax#2019 redirect warning in `checkModelResolution` (stored credential sent to `baseUrl`) is left as is, including its wording for introduced providers.
